title: Nearest Cake on a Line
description_html:
Given a binary array A on a line where A[i] = 0 is a person at index i and A[i] = 1 is a cake, each person eats the nearest cake (distance = absolute index difference). It is guaranteed no person is tied between two cakes and no cake between two people, so the assignment is unique.

Given A and a person index p (A[p] = 0), output the index of the cake that person p eats, or -1 if there is no cake.

Input

n, then a 0/1 string of length n, then p

Output

One integer: the eaten cake's index, or -1.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5.

Example

5
10010
1
----
0

Person at index 1: nearest cake is index 0 (distance 1) vs index 3 (distance 2) → eats 0.

1D nearest-target (cf. LC 821); the line companion of #10059. See Notes.
